Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To better understand your chronic left shoulder pain, could you describe the nature of the pain—is it sharp, dull, or aching? Also, does the pain radiate to your neck, arm, or chest, and are there any specific movements that make it worse?
Klaus Mueller

The pain feels like a deep, constant ache that gets sharper when I try to reach behind my back or overhead. It doesn't radiate to my neck or arm, but it definitely keeps me from sleeping on that side. Simple things like brushing my hair or putting on a shirt have become really difficult lately.
Maria Lopez

The pain is a dull ache that radiates to my neck and left arm, especially when I raise my arm or sleep on that side. It gets worse at night, sometimes waking me up. I don't have any numbness or tingling, but the pain has been constant for about six months. I have high blood pressure and high cholesterol, but no history of heart problems. I work as an office clerk and sit at a computer most of the day.
Klaus Mueller

Actually, that description doesn't match my condition at all; my pain has been present for only two months, not six, and I do not have high blood pressure. I have type 2 diabetes, but the pain stays right in my shoulder without radiating to my neck or arm. As I mentioned, it's specifically the extreme ranges of motion that trigger the sharp pain and make dressing difficult.
Maria Lopez

Do you experience any shortness of breath, jaw pain, or unusual fatigue during physical exertion, given your history of high blood pressure and cholesterol? Also, do you notice any stiffness in the morning that lasts more than an hour, or have you experienced recent weight loss or fever?
Klaus Mueller

No, I do not have shortness of breath, jaw pain, or unusual fatigue, and I would like to correct that I do not have high blood pressure or cholesterol issues; my only known condition is type 2 diabetes. I do not experience morning stiffness that lasts longer than an hour, nor do I have any recent weight loss or fever. My symptoms are strictly limited to the deep ache in my left shoulder that worsens with movement and disrupts my sleep.
Maria Lopez

No, I don't experience shortness of breath, jaw pain, or unusual fatigue, and I haven't had any morning stiffness lasting over an hour, weight loss, or fever. My main issue is just that persistent ache.

I see. Has the pain been accompanied by any weakness in your left arm, or have you noticed any clicking or popping sounds when you move your shoulder? Also, do you have any history of thyroid issues or diabetes?
Klaus Mueller

I haven't noticed any weakness, clicking, or popping in my arm, but I do have type 2 diabetes which I manage with medication. The pain remains localized to my shoulder without any neurological symptoms like numbness.
Maria Lopez

No, I haven't noticed any weakness, clicking, or popping, and I have no history of thyroid issues or diabetes. The pain just seems to be a constant, nagging ache.

Given the radiation to your arm and the nighttime aggravation, do you experience any pain specifically between your shoulder blades or in the inner part of your left arm, and does the pain worsen when you cough, sneeze, or take a deep breath?
Klaus Mueller

No, I do not have pain between my shoulder blades or in the inner part of my arm, and my symptoms do not worsen when I cough, sneeze, or take a deep breath. The pain is strictly localized to my left shoulder and is only triggered by extreme movements like reaching overhead or dressing. I want to reiterate that I have type 2 diabetes but no history of thyroid issues, and the pain has been present for two months, not six.
Maria Lopez

No, the pain does not worsen with coughing, sneezing, or deep breaths, and there is no specific pain between the shoulder blades or in the inner arm beyond the general ache. I do not have any recent infections or fevers either.

Given your risk factors and the nature of the pain radiating down the arm without mechanical symptoms, I need to rule out cardiac involvement before focusing on musculoskeletal causes. Electrocardiogram (EKG) and Echocardiogram.

I have received the EKG and Echocardiogram results, which show no evidence of cardiac ischemia or structural heart disease. Since the pain is nocturnal, radiates to the neck and arm, and lacks mechanical symptoms like clicking, could you confirm if you have any history of repetitive overhead activities or if the pain ever feels like it originates deep inside the shoulder joint itself?
Klaus Mueller

I must clarify that my pain does not radiate to my neck or arm; it stays strictly within my left shoulder. There is no history of repetitive overhead activities, but the pain does feel deep inside the joint, especially when I try to reach up or behind my back.
Maria Lopez
Do you perform any repetitive overhead activities, and does the pain feel like it originates deep within the shoulder joint rather than the surrounding muscles?
